items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: the leader of the band was a woman from New York named Marie Lucas... So I played, got that job. Now man, I got that job and I stayed on that job for three years

ctx.x: is a weekend, and my first day in Washington, D. C., I'm in the poolroom. They had a pool hall right next to the Howard Theatre in Washington, D. C. 7th and T, still there. I'm playing pool, about 12:00 in the morning, a guy come busting in the poolroom and say, 'Can anybody here play drums?' So I say, I can. He say, well, come on, I got a job, the drummer, his wife, he had to leave town, because his wife -- he's back in the alimony. Guy named Cootie Perkins, went to Canada. He's still there.

So I went in the theatre and they had an all Puerto Rican band except the piano player, he was American. And the leader of the band was a woman from New York named Marie Lucas. She used to play the Lafayette Theatre here on Seventh Ave. famous theatre, and she was director, oh, man, she was (unintell.) so I played, got that job.

Now man, I got that job and I stayed on that job for three years, playing in the pit, but in the meantime they had a little group down in Washington, I forget their names. They played a private club from 11:30 to 1:30, private club, very rich people. I got that job, singing and playing. I'm through at the theatre at ten. So I double, I guess I was the first drummer in Washington to double on jobs at one time. I got that job, and now I'm making money hand over fist. Ain't married, ain't nothing on my mind but my…
